name: Tool-Planner: Task Planning with Clusters across Multiple Tools
venue: ICLR 2025 (arXiv preprint 2406.03807, first submitted Jun 2024; camera-ready accepted to The Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations 2025)
authors_affiliation: Yanming Liu, Xinyue Peng, Jiannan Cao, Shi Bo, Yuwei Zhang, Xuhong Zhang, Sheng Cheng, Xun Wang, Jianwei Yin, Tianyu Du. Lead/primary affiliation: Zhejiang University (with Southeast University and Massachusetts Institute of Technology). Corresponding authors at ZJU.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/OceannTwT/Tool-Planner (official repo; OpenReview forum: https://openreview.net/forum?id=dRz3cizftU). Not a continuously-updated leaderboard/paper-list; it is the method's own code repository.
task_domain: tool-use (LLM tool learning: task planning and multi-tool/API invocation)
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent LLM tool learning over large real-world API pools (ToolBench/RapidAPI, APIBench). The LLM must plan a multi-step solution and invoke external APIs, observing execution feedback (errors) and re-planning when tools fail. No retriever or planner training: the backbone LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude-3) are used off-the-shelf; the only learned component is an off-the-shelf SimCSE encoder used offline to cluster tools. Supervision for the method itself is none; evaluation uses ToolEval-style judging.
what_is_retrieved: tools / APIs, organized as toolkits (clusters of same-function APIs). At plan time the model selects toolkits (a set of functionally-equivalent tools per node); at execution/error time it selects an alternative concrete API from within the current toolkit.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus of tool/API documentation and descriptions (ToolBench RapidAPI APIs, APIBench model-hub APIs). The toolkit clusters are induced offline and remain fixed during task solving; no growing/episodic memory is written back.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness-of-the-needed-set oriented rather than a fixed top-k ranking: each node is a whole toolkit (set of functionally-equivalent APIs) so the planner aims to exhaustively exhaust functionally-equivalent alternatives within a node before abandoning a path, maximizing recovery of a working tool for each subtask rather than ranking one best tool.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning). If forced to map: [Retrieve: yes (select toolkit/API), Reuse: yes (reuse alternative within toolkit), Revise: partial (re-select tool / replan across toolkits on error), Retain: no (no case stored back)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is positioned as tree-search-based task planning over tool clusters.
retrieval_unit: tool-API (single API) grouped into a cluster/toolkit. The retrievable/planning unit is the toolkit (cluster of functionally-equivalent APIs); the executable unit is an individual tool-API selected from within that toolkit.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced. Tool/API documentation and descriptions are summarized by an LLM into functionality explanations, embedded with SimCSE, then clustered offline with k-means++ into toolkits before task solving. No online/test-time growth of the store.
index_structure_topology: cluster-or-toolkit organization: APIs are grouped into k clusters (toolkits) of same/similar function via k-means++ over SimCSE embeddings. During solving, planning forms a decision/behavior tree G(T)=(V_T, E_T) whose nodes are toolkits, so the effective structure is cluster-keyed nodes arranged in a search tree.
retriever_type: dense (SimCSE sentence-embedding similarity) for offline tool clustering, combined with LLM-as-selector at plan/execution time (the LLM chooses which toolkit and which API within a toolkit). No BM25/learned-to-rank retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf): SimCSE is a pretrained contrastive sentence encoder used as-is (princeton-nlp/sup-simcse-roberta-base); k-means++ is unsupervised. Tool selection within/across toolkits is performed by the frozen LLM via prompting, not a trained retrieval policy. The contrastive signal exists only inside the pretrained SimCSE encoder, not trained for this task.
query_construction: Plan-time: the LLM generates a multi-step plan over toolkit functionality descriptions m_{T_h}=f(T_h) given the user instruction x and tool docs/descriptions D,M. Error-time: when an API fails, the current state plus error information E and the retained plan condition the choice of an alternative API within the same toolkit, or a new cross-toolkit plan. Clustering query/key: LLM-generated functionality explanations H={h_i} embedded by SimCSE.
query_granularity: Two-level: task-level (initial toolkit-level plan over the whole instruction) and step/state-level (per-node selection of a concrete API within the current toolkit, and per-error re-selection/replanning).
when_to_retrieve: iterative / active (error-triggered): toolkit clustering is one-shot offline; tool (re)selection is iterative during execution and is actively triggered when a tool invocation error / unavailability occurs.
retrieval_trigger_signal: agent/execution-feedback-initiated: a tool invocation error (invalid/missing parameters, false API call format, API hallucinated, tool unavailable) triggers reselection of an alternative API within the same toolkit; if all APIs in the toolkit fail, the accumulated error information E triggers cross-toolkit replanning on the subgraph G(T) minus the failed node.
reranking: No explicit learned reranking stage. Within-toolkit alternative selection is done by the LLM among functionally-equivalent APIs; clusters are formed by k-means++ over SimCSE similarity (no cross-encoder / RRF reranker).
retrieved_context_refinement: Light: tool documentation and descriptions are summarized by an LLM into brief functionality explanations before embedding/clustering (decompose-then-summarize style). At solving time the planner sees toolkit functionality descriptions rather than full per-API docs (a form of abstraction/compression); no distractor-filtering or reason-in-documents distillation module.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation + tool reuse: toolkit functionality descriptions and candidate APIs are placed in the LLM prompt to drive planning and tool calls; on failure, an alternative API from the same toolkit is reused without altering the plan structure (E_T kept unchanged), keeping plan stability.
planning_integration: Inside a decision/behavior tree search. Tool-Planner conceptualizes problem solving as a decision tree where each node is a toolkit (set of tools). Plan-then-act with error-driven replanning: (a) within-toolkit reselection on a single tool failure keeps the plan path fixed; (b) cross-toolkit replanning (DFSDT-style depth-first search but at the toolkit level rather than the individual-API level) when all APIs in a toolkit fail, on subgraph G(T)<-G(T)\v.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-tool-call within a rollout: retrieval/selection is woven in at each tool invocation step (choose an API for the current toolkit node, and re-select on error), with coarser task-level replanning across toolkits when a node fully fails.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR adaptation). The closest analog: execution-feedback-driven revision — on tool failure the LLM re-selects an alternative API within the toolkit (verbatim swap of equivalent tool) or, if exhausted, prompts the LLM to generate a new cross-toolkit plan using error information while retaining prior states.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form injected into the prompt is structured/free-text tool information: toolkit functionality descriptions m_{T_h}=f(T_h) plus candidate API documentation/descriptions; the executable form is the concrete API call (function name + parameters).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Reusable functional grouping: a toolkit is an abstracted cluster of functionally-equivalent APIs described by a shared functionality explanation (more abstract than a single raw API document but not a distilled strategy/workflow). The unit ranges from this abstracted toolkit (plan level) down to a single procedural tool/API (execution level).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Functional clustering provides redundancy/robustness: if a chosen API fails or hallucinates, equivalent APIs in the same toolkit serve as fallbacks, reducing the impact of a single bad/unavailable tool. A 'Cluster Incomplete' error (~13.5% of analyzed errors) is acknowledged as a failure mode where clustering misses relevant APIs. No retriever-aware SFT or self-reflection relevance evaluator beyond LLM error handling.
memory_type: none (no persistent learned memory). The toolkit/cluster index is a static offline-built tool library, not an episodic/skill memory that evolves.
write_back: False. No new experiences, cases, or skills are written back to a memory store; clusters are fixed after offline induction and intermediate results are used only within the current task's solution tree.
online_growth: No. The toolkit store is frozen after offline SimCSE+k-means++ clustering; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
failure_experience_usage: Within-episode only: failure/error information E={F_t(t_e)} from failed API calls is fed back to the LLM to trigger within-toolkit reselection and cross-toolkit replanning during the same task. Failures are NOT stored persistently across tasks; there is no success+failure contrastive memory or corrective rule database.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored entries are mutated; the cluster index is static after offline construction).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Tool/toolkit selection is performed by the frozen LLM via prompting plus fixed SimCSE-similarity clustering; it is not an RL/value-based or otherwise learned retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent framework; no memory/experience sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: ToolBench (sub-datasets G1-Inst, G1-Tool, G1-Cat, G2-Inst, G2-Cat, G3-Inst; APIs from RapidAPI Hub, 16,464 APIs) and APIBench (TorchHub, HuggingFace, TensorFlow; 1,645 selected APIs).
baselines: ReAct (Yao et al. 2022), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), AdaPlanner (Sun et al. 2023a), DFSDT (Qin et al. 2024, ToolLLM). Ablation also compares ReAct+Toolkit and AdaPlanner+Toolkit. Backbone LLMs: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0125), GPT-4 (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09), Claude-3 (claude-3-sonnet).
key_metrics: Pass Rate (%), Win Rate (%) (ToolEval-style LLM judgment vs GPT-3.5+ReAct), Hallucination Rate (%) (APIBench), and efficiency: average running time (sec) / latency and re-planning frequency.
headline_result: On ToolBench with GPT-4, Tool-Planner improves average Pass Rate by +8.8% and Win Rate by +9.1% over the strongest baseline DFSDT (avg Pass 77.3% vs 68.5%, avg Win 77.5% vs 68.4%); on APIBench with GPT-4 it gains +6.6% pass and +14.5% win. Reported latency only ~2x ReAct/AdaPlanner while DFSDT is 6-8x.
ablations: (1) Tool clustering ablation: adding the clustering-derived toolkit to baselines (ReAct+Toolkit, AdaPlanner+Toolkit) on GPT-4 raises pass/win across G1-Tool/G2-Inst/G2-Cat/G3-Inst (e.g., G1-Tool pass +9.0%, G3-Inst win +4.3%); AdaPlanner+Toolkit even slightly exceeds DFSDT, showing the toolkit node design drives gains. (2) Number of clusters k: best when average cluster size ~9 on G1-inst (k=1800 ToolBench, k=65 APIBench); too large k under-clusters (slow, incomplete exploration), too small k mixes functions (wrong tool calls). (3) Text embedding model for clustering: SimCSE > text-embedding-ada-02 > Contriever > RoBERTa-base on pass rate (e.g., G1-inst 66.0 vs 63.5/61.0/60.5). (4) Efficiency: running-time comparison vs ReAct/AdaPlanner/DFSDT. (5) Error analysis: Invalid Input Parameters most frequent; Cluster Incomplete ~13.5%.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Intrinsic retrieval/clustering metrics (e.g., Recall@k / nDCG) are not reported separately; evaluation is end-to-end task metrics (Pass/Win/Hallucination Rate) plus efficiency. Clustering quality is probed only indirectly via downstream pass rate across embedding models and k values.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both: outcome metrics (Pass/Win/Hallucination Rate) plus process-quality signals — re-planning frequency, average running time/latency, and an error-type distribution analysis (process diagnostics) rather than only final success.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported as a core selling point: Tool-Planner reduces re-planning frequency and computation. Latency is only ~2x that of linear methods (ReAct/AdaPlanner) versus DFSDT's 6-8x, because on a tool error it swaps in a same-function API within the toolkit without discarding/re-searching the whole path. Quantified via average running time (sec) per dataset (Figure 4).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Implicit/abstraction-driven rather than a fixed token cap: at plan time the model conditions on toolkit functionality descriptions (compressed vs full per-API docs) so multiple equivalent APIs are represented compactly; number of clusters k controls granularity (k=1800 ToolBench avg cluster size ~9; k=65 APIBench). No explicit injected-token budget reported. [uncertain] exact prompt token budget.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Uses existing benchmarks: ToolBench (16,464 RapidAPI APIs, G1/G2/G3 = single-tool / intra-category multi-tool / intra-collection multi-tool instructions) and APIBench (1,645 APIs from TorchHub/HuggingFace/TensorFlow). Tool-Planner does not construct a new benchmark; answer verifiability follows ToolEval (Pass Rate) and pairwise Win Rate judging.
builds_on: DFSDT / ToolLLM (Qin et al. 2024) — extends DFSDT's depth-first solution-tree search by replacing per-API nodes with toolkit (cluster) nodes; SimCSE (Gao et al. 2021) for tool embeddings; k-means++ (Arthur & Vassilvitskii 2007) for clustering; ToolBench (Qin et al. 2024) and APIBench/Gorilla (Patil et al. 2023) datasets; Tree-Planner (Hu et al. 2023) and tree-of-thought lineage for tree-structured planning.
contrasts_with: ReAct (linear tool use), Reflexion (verbal feedback re-planning at API level), AdaPlanner (point error correction), DFSDT (API-level depth-first re-planning that discards failing paths). Also contrasts with CRITIC and AnyTool feedback-integration methods and with MCTS/Toolchain* search; key contrast is toolkit-level (cluster) reselection/replanning vs single-API-level search.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): tree-search task-planning over clustered tool stores. Lineage: ReAct -> Reflexion/AdaPlanner -> DFSDT (ToolLLM) -> Tool-Planner, advancing from single-API tree search to cluster/toolkit-level planning with within-cluster fallback retrieval and cross-cluster replanning.
tool_document_engineering: LLM-generated functionality explanations: raw API documentation D and descriptions M are summarized by an LLM into brief functionality explanations H={h_i}, which are then embedded by SimCSE for clustering (a summary/expansion step rather than raw-docstring embedding or instruction-tuned tool embeddings).
index_content_separation: Partial / abstraction-based: at plan time the model reasons over compact toolkit functionality descriptions (the lightweight index), while heavier per-API documentation d_t' is consulted on demand when generating call parameters for a specific selected API — a form of progressive disclosure (functionality-index then per-API content).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index built offline via SimCSE+k-means++ clustering (no live CRUD auto-sync). Integration protocol is RapidAPI (ToolBench) plus model-hub APIs (APIBench); execution uses the ToolBench RapidAPI calling interface. Not MCP; no live-synchronized tool store.
tool_dependency_awareness: Limited: clustering captures functional EQUIVALENCE (interchangeable same-function APIs) rather than inter-tool DEPENDENCIES (output-of-A feeds B / shared auth / prerequisites). Sequential dependencies are handled by the LLM-generated decision-tree plan (state outputs feed the next state), but there is no explicit dependency graph or dependency-aware reranking. [uncertain] whether any implicit dependency modeling exists.
